speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. You mention a chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; to understand the underlying cause, how many packs of cigarettes do you smoke per day, if any? Additionally, have you ever noticed symptoms like weight loss, night sweats, or coughing up blood?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis. The patient's 11-year history of a chronic cough with copious, thick, purulent sputum (yellow-green) that worsens in the morning, combined with recurrent bronchitis requiring antibiotics and a non-smoking status, strongly points to bronchiectasis. I am requesting a Chest_X-Ray and CT_Chest to confirm bronchial dilation and rule out other causes.
